references.text: The burnt offering shall be a bull or a lamb without defect, as described in the laws for burnt offerings in Leviticus.
A one-year-old lamb without defect is used as a burnt offering, with the same requirements as in the consecration offering.
The sacrificial animals must be without defect to be accepted: a bull, ram, or male goat.
The same offering was given by Nahshon son of Amminadab on the first day—a young bull, a ram, and a one-year-old lamb for a burnt offering.
Nethanel son of Zuar gave the same burnt offering on the second day.
Eliab son of Helon gave the same burnt offering on the third day.
Elisur son of Shedeur gave the same burnt offering on the fourth day.
One-year-old lambs without defect are used as burnt offerings during the festivals.
One-year-old lambs shall be offered daily as a burnt offering on the altar.
